quote: Alright. I had something. You guys just emailed me a quote over.
stewart_read: Customer references a prior emailed quote as their very first substantive line on the call — this is competitive/prior-touch intelligence the rep never asks about.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged this as small talk not worth pursuing given the call's brevity, but the comment is specific enough (a quote already sent) that it likely represents a real prior touchpoint worth 15 seconds of probing.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to ask a single follow-up — 'oh which design did you get, do you remember the numbers?' — before moving into verify. Costs nothing and surfaces whether Ion already has data on this lead.

quote: Oh, I just I'm with the design team. I help, like, get you their design going so we can find out what we can offer you.
stewart_read: The customer's comment about an emailed quote directly questioned what this call even is, and the rep's answer is vague filler that doesn't explain why he's calling now or reference the form submission per the standard intro script.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be improvising because the customer interrupted the scripted intro before it was fully delivered, which is a legitimate constraint rather than a skipped step.
coaching_implication: When a customer interrupts the intro with confusion, the rep should still land the legitimacy anchor ('you filled out a form, I'm following up on the design that comes from that') instead of a vague filler line.

quote: Black Hills. Those are some of the questions on your fucking questionnaire.
stewart_read: This is a sharp irritation spike mid-verify — likely fatigue from repetitive-feeling questions layered on top of the unresolved quote confusion from 00:13. The rep does not acknowledge the tone at all and moves straight to the next question.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged the outburst as not customer-directed hostility (frustration at process, not at him) and correctly chose not to derail momentum by dwelling on it.
coaching_implication: A one-line acknowledgment ('I know, these questions can feel repetitive — just a couple more and I've got what I need') costs 3 seconds and prevents frustration from compounding into the DQ moment at 02:15.

quote: And then your roof, you know what kind it is?
stewart_read: The roof question is asked as a flat checklist item immediately after the bill figure was captured, with no acknowledgment of the $340/month number the customer just gave.
alternative_hypothesis: Given how quickly the call ends afterward (DQ within 15 seconds), there may not have been a real window to flip the bill before the ground-mount disclosure ended the call.
coaching_implication: Even in short calls, capturing a bill figure without any verbal acknowledgment (e.g., '$340, okay, that's a solid number to work with') is a missed low-cost anchor — habitual, not just situational here.

quote: I don't want it mounted on my roof. I got five acres. I like it mounted on the ground.
stewart_read: Five acres and an explicit ground-mount preference signal a customer who has already thought about system placement and land use — normally a sign of higher engagement — but it collides directly with Ion's roof-only capability.
alternative_hypothesis: This could also be read purely as a disqualifying fact with no enthusiasm value, since Ion cannot act on it regardless of how engaged the customer is.
coaching_implication: Nothing actionable for THIS deal since ground mount is a hard capability gap, but worth noting for lead-source quality conversations — this customer was substantively engaged with solar concepts, just for a product Ion doesn't build.

quote: Okay. We only do roofs and many like, residential roofs for the home. We can't do ground mounts.
stewart_read: The rep correctly and honestly discloses the hard capability gap rather than stringing the customer along toward a doomed appointment — this is the right procedural call, not a persuasion failure. Ion's schema does not currently list a ground-mount dq_rule explicitly, which is a schema gap worth flagging rather than a rep error.
alternative_hypothesis: A reactive read would call this a missed save attempt, but there is no rebuttal available for a genuine product-capability gap — pushing further would risk booking an appointment destined to fail at proposal.
coaching_implication: No coaching needed on the rep's honesty here; flag to Kenny that ground-mount-only preference is an undocumented hard DQ and should be added to dq_rules explicitly so future analysis doesn't misclassify it.
